source_title: Opposition Meets at Kharge's Residence, Plans Public Impeachment of CEC - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
Leaders from the INDIA bloc gathered at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi for a strategy meeting to plan a public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The venue was relocated to Kharge's official residence after permissions were reportedly denied for earlier locations, including Hotel Ashoka. The planned public proceedings are structured to reflect parliamentary functioning, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar expected to preside over the session. The meeting was attended by senior opposition figures, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Derek O'Brien, Jairam Ramesh, and John Brittas. Leaders highlighted that representatives from opposition parties and civil society will participate, with motions to be moved and discussed by the Leaders of Opposition from both Houses. Rahul Gandhi Urges People To Join Chalo Dilli March At Ramlila Maidan
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has issued a call for the Chalo Dilli protest march scheduled for 1st November at Ramlila Maidan. Describing it as a march for the soul of the country and a Save Democracy initiative, he urged citizens, opposition workers, and student groups across political lines to participate. Addressing the public, he asserted that people should not worry about police lathis and stated that the march aims to protect the Constitution and protest against alleged vote theft. India Today correspondent Moushumi Singh reported that the rally represents an attempt by the India Bloc to build momentum and mobilise public support ahead of a public impeachment planned at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence. The demonstration is expected to see participation from civil society and opposition party workers arriving from neighbouring states including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, and Haryana.
Rahul Gandhi: 'Election Commission Is Not Functioning As The Election Commission Of India'
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticised the Election Commission, alleging it is not functioning as the Election Commission of India and is not doing its job. He claimed to have 'concrete 100% proof of Election Commission allowing cheating in a seat in Karnataka', asserting this pattern is occurring across constituency after constituency. Gandhi alleged irregularities in voter addition and deletion, claiming thousands of new voters aged 45 to 65 were added in a single constituency.
Row Over SIR: Karnataka Minister Backs Voter Deletions, Rahul Gandhi Opposes, BJP Mocks
A major political controversy has emerged as Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi defended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka, differing from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's nationwide stance. Jarkiholi maintained that the enumeration and deletion of nearly one crore voters in Karnataka was properly conducted, removing duplicate, relocated, and deceased electors. He stated that the party's objections were focused on states such as West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Bihar. In contrast, Rahul Gandhi has fiercely attacked the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the drive, alleging vote rigging and the disenfranchisement of genuine voters while demanding the exercise be halted. The divergence has triggered attacks from the Bharatiya Janata Party, which claimed Congress leaders are exposing Rahul Gandhi's claims. Meanwhile, other Congress leaders have questioned the Karnataka deletions, citing reports of living electors being erroneously marked as dead and reaffirming full backing for Rahul Gandhi's nationwide campaign.
BJP Mocks Congress Over Ballot Paper Defeat in MLC Polls Amid 'Vote Chori' Row
The Bharatiya Janata Party has launched a sharp attack against the Congress following the outcome of the Legislative Council elections across four states, where polling was conducted using ballot papers. Highlighting that the Congress secured only one seat while the BJP won 16 out of 28 seats, the party questioned the opposition's ongoing 'vote chori' campaign against electronic voting machines. Party leaders stated that the Congress has consistently demanded a return to paper ballots, yet failed to secure voter backing when ballot papers were actually deployed. Union Minister and BJP President JP Nadda criticised the opposition's conduct, saying political credibility must be established with verifiable facts before approaching the Election Commission instead of raising unproven allegations over voter rolls. In response, Congress leaders such as Pawan Khera challenged the government to conduct the upcoming assembly elections using ballot papers if the BJP is truly confident.
